rules.title: Shares (DM sends) outrank likes by a wide margin — build for the send, not the like
rules.action: Build the Reel around a moment a fan would DM to one friend
rules.rule: Design Reels around a moment a fan would forward to one specific friend (e.g., tagging a friend with 'we need to go to this' or 'this is so us'), not around maximizing likes. Treat the caption's job as prompting a send, and check 'sends per reach' in Insights as a primary health metric alongside watch time.
rules.insight: Shares/DM-sends are weighted far above likes in Instagram's ranking — Mosseri has named sends-per-reach as a top signal, and one 2026 study estimates roughly 4x the weighting of likes.
rules.evidence: Adam Mosseri has repeatedly named watch time, sends per reach, and likes per reach as the top cross-surface ranking signals (confirmed via his own Reels/posts, e.g. instagram.com/p/DFFyRp-pINJ, referenced by Hootsuite). Multiple 2026 industry analyses (Later, Hootsuite, Hypebot citing an April 2026 Podswap reverse-engineering study of 2,500+ niches) converge on shares/DM-sends being weighted several times higher than likes for distribution beyond the initial audience, with one estimate of roughly 4x weighting and a 'share-to-DM velocity' signal. Re-verified 2026-09-08: 2026 coverage continues to report Mosseri stating shares/sends are the single most important signal, and 'sends per reach' appears in every 2026 restatement of Instagram's confirmed top-three Reels signals (watch time, sends per reach, likes per reach). No change to the rule.

rules.title: Saves are the second-strongest signal — give fans a reason to bookmark, not just watch
rules.action: Give fans something worth bookmarking, not just watching
rules.rule: Publish some content with clear 'utility' a fan would save to revisit — set-list previews, a chord/lyric snippet, 'venues I love playing in Colorado,' behind-the-scenes gear or songwriting notes. Don't make every post pure performance footage; mix in save-worthy carousels alongside Reels.
rules.insight: Saves became a top-tier ranking signal in a 2026 update — carousels with real utility (setlists, lyric snippets, gear notes) earn 3-4x the save rate of comparable Reels.
rules.evidence: Multiple 2026 sources report saves were elevated to a top-tier ranking signal in a 2026 update (one source cites a February 2026 Instagram Creator Education post ranking saves above comments and near watch time). Carousels in particular are documented to earn 3-4x the save rate of a comparable Reel from educational/utility accounts, per Socialinsider-style benchmark analysis.

rules.title: Small accounts are not disadvantaged — a strong Reel from a small profile can match a big account's reach, but it must clear sequential 'trial' gates
rules.action: Post 3-5 Reels a week and let each one clear its first-hour test
rules.rule: Post consistently (aim for 3-5 Reels/week — Instagram needs enough volume to run its tests) and treat every Reel's first hour as a gate: if it doesn't get strong early watch-time/save/share signal from your existing (small) audience, it won't advance to the non-follower test pool. Use Trial Reels deliberately to test hooks/formats against cold (non-follower) audiences before deciding whether to promote a video further.
rules.insight: Trial Reels test every video against cold, non-follower audiences before widening distribution — engagement quality beats audience size under roughly 50K followers. Instagram's own audition system now also applies this staged-exposure model to regular (non-Trial) Reels.
rules.evidence: Instagram's own Trial Reels feature (help.instagram.com/1013292530224018, and creators.instagram.com/blog/instagram-trial-reels) is designed explicitly to show a Reel to non-followers first and gauge performance before wider distribution — confirmed by Instagram's Help Center and its own Creators blog. As of Feb 2026, Trial Reels can be scheduled in advance (Social Media Today), and Instagram requires each Trial Reel be a genuinely unique upload rather than a repeated re-test of the same clip. Industry write-ups describe a broader 'audition system' for all Reels: a small initial non-follower exposure round, then a wider audition, then full distribution if early signal holds — reinforcing that the first-hour test matters beyond Trial Reels specifically. Multiple sources agree follower count under ~50K is 'the sweet spot' where engagement quality, not audience size, determines reach. A claimed numeric daily cap on Trial Reels (~5/day, 30-day suspension for exceeding it) appears only on lower-tier aggregator sites and is not corroborated by a primary or second independent source — treat as unverified, do not rely on the exact numbers.

rules.title: TikTok watermarks and recycled/reposted content are actively suppressed
rules.action: Never post a Reel with a TikTok or CapCut watermark still on it
rules.rule: Never cross-post a Reel that still carries a TikTok (or CapCut) watermark/logo — re-export clean, native-resolution vertical video for Instagram. Avoid re-uploading the identical Reel repeatedly; Instagram's originality detection can exclude accounts with heavy repost patterns from recommendations entirely.
rules.insight: Instagram's originality detection actively suppresses watermarked or heavily-reposted content — some 2026 sources describe a numeric threshold (10+ reposts in 30 days) triggering full exclusion from Explore/recommendations, not just down-ranking, though this exact number is not yet Meta-confirmed.
rules.evidence: Instagram's own creator guidance (Mosseri's posted 'Reels basics' video, referenced across Hootsuite/Later) explicitly lists 'non-watermarked, original content' as a baseline requirement for recommendation eligibility. Multiple 2026 sources describe an 'Originality Score' and cite accounts with 10+ reposts in 30 days being excluded from recommendations entirely (not merely suppressed); watermarked reposts are described as actively detected and suppressed. The specific '10 reposts/30 days' threshold is repeated across aggregator sources (MeetEdgar, CreatorFlow) as of this pass but still lacks a Meta primary-source citation — treat the exclusion mechanism as real, the exact number as directional only. Re-verified 2026-09-08: 2026 syntheses continue to describe AI fingerprinting of content first posted elsewhere, with original-to-Instagram content reported as receiving materially more distribution than repurposed content. rules.title: External links in captions quietly cut reach; keep links out of captions and use bio / Stories link sticker instead
rules.action: Keep links out of captions — use the bio link or a Stories sticker
rules.rule: Never put megcmusic.com or ticket/merch links directly in a Reel or feed caption. Route traffic via the bio link or a Stories link sticker instead. The literal phrase 'link in bio' does not hurt reach — it's the actual clickable URL in the caption that does.
rules.insight: An outbound URL in a caption costs an estimated 19-60% of reach; saying "link in bio" doesn't hurt — only an actual clickable link does.
rules.evidence: Multiple 2026 analyses estimate reach penalties from in-caption external links ranging from ~19% lower median reach up to 40-60% reduction versus an otherwise identical linkless post, attributed to Instagram's preference for keeping users in-app. Separately, Mosseri has explicitly debunked the idea that saying 'link in bio' (the phrase itself) hurts reach — the penalty is tied to the presence of an actual outbound URL, not the words used to reference it.

rules.title: Engagement bait (comment-to-unlock, tag-3-friends, follow-for-follow) caps a post at its seed audience and can drag account-level trust
rules.action: Skip comment-to-unlock and tag-3-friends prompts
rules.rule: Avoid transactional prompts like 'comment YES for the link' or 'tag 3 friends who need this' — use open-ended questions instead (which still perform fine). Reserve CTAs for genuine calls to action (e.g., 'which song should I play at the show Friday?') rather than manipulative engagement loops.
rules.insight: Meta's Transparency Center explicitly demotes engagement bait — the post caps at its seed audience, and a pattern of bait captions drags the whole account's trust over time.
rules.evidence: Meta's own Transparency Center has a dedicated Engagement Bait policy page defining and penalizing this pattern (confirmed primary source, though the fetched page returned only metadata with the core content behind further navigation). Independent 2026 analyses describe the mechanism as post-level demotion (the post stays capped in its seed audience) with a slower account-level 'drag' effect from a pattern of bait captions — corroborated by two independent industry write-ups.

rules.title: Raw, human-shot content is outperforming polished/AI-flavored production, and Instagram is explicitly deprioritizing low-authenticity AI content in 2026
rules.action: Lead with a raw, human moment in the first 1.5-3 seconds
rules.rule: Favor phone-shot, imperfect rehearsal clips, backstage moments, and human-voiced intros over highly produced music-video-style edits. Lead Reels with a spoken hook or visible human perspective in the first 1.5-3 seconds rather than a polished montage; use Trial Reels to test which raw clips earn distribution before committing studio-quality edits.
rules.insight: Mosseri's 2026 year-end memo explicitly prioritizes raw, human content over polished or AI-flavored production — one study found phone-shot visuals outperforming studio edits by roughly 35% in discovery feeds.

rules.title: Collab posts (co-published with a co-billed artist, opener, or venue) share reach across both accounts' audiences

rules.title: Instagram's 'Your Algorithm' controls are now live across Feed, Reels, and Explore — discovery is increasingly user-directed, not just engagement-signal-driven
rules.action: Give fans an explicit reason to mark content 'more like this,' don't rely on signals alone
rules.rule: Beyond passive engagement signals (shares, saves, watch time), users can now directly tell Instagram to see more or less of specific topics across Feed, Reels, and Explore (fully rolled out June 2026). Since recommendations increasingly reflect user-chosen topic preferences rather than a single static ranking, consider occasionally inviting engaged fans (in captions or Stories) to tap 'more like this' on posts they enjoy, and don't assume a strong early engagement signal alone guarantees continued distribution if it doesn't align with a user's chosen topics.
rules.insight: Instagram's 'Your Algorithm' feature is now a unified system spanning Feed, Reels, and Explore — discovery is shifting from a single ranking model toward user-directed topic control, which can help genre-aligned creators but makes reach less predictable.
rules.evidence: Instagram's official blog (about.instagram.com) confirms 'Your Algorithm' debuted on Reels in December 2025, expanded to Explore in April 2026, and rolled out across Feed, Reels, and Explore globally in June 2026 as 'one unified system' — adjustments a user makes ripple across all three surfaces. Independent coverage (TechCrunch, Social Media Today) corroborates the June 2026 Feed expansion and notes it lets users tell the algorithm what topics to show more or less of directly, rather than relying solely on implicit engagement signals. Re-verified 2026-09-08: September 2026 coverage describes 'Your Algorithm' as still actively rolling out to all English-speaking users on the main Feed, and secondary sources disagree on the first-test date (October vs December 2025). rules.title: The upload cap is 20 minutes but the discovery cap is about 3 — Reels over ~3 minutes are effectively follower-only
rules.action: Cut any Reel meant to reach new people to under 90 seconds
rules.rule: Instagram now accepts Reels up to 20 minutes filmed in the in-app camera and up to 15 minutes uploaded from the camera roll, but length decides who sees it, not just how long they watch. Under ~90 seconds gives the best chance of landing on the Reels tab and reaching non-followers; 90 seconds to 3 minutes still plays well to existing followers with weaker cold reach; over 3 minutes is generally not pushed to people who don't already follow the account. Treat full-song performances, story-behind-the-song cuts and livestream pulls as follower-facing content, and cut a separate sub-90-second hook clip whenever the goal is a new fan rather than a deeper one. Camera-roll uploads that exceed the in-app limit are also flagged as not prioritised by the Reels algorithm, so film long pieces in-app where practical.
rules.insight: The number Instagram will accept and the number Instagram will recommend are different: 20 minutes is the upload ceiling, roughly 3 minutes is where non-follower distribution stops.
rules.evidence: Buffer's Instagram Reels length guide (current 2026 content) states Reels run from 15 seconds to 20 minutes when filmed in the Instagram camera and up to 15 minutes when uploaded from the camera roll, that under-90-second Reels have the 'highest chance of landing on the reels tab and reaching new audiences', that 90 seconds to three minutes brings 'slightly lower reach but stronger watch time from loyal followers', and that Reels over three minutes 'aren't typically pushed to non-followers'; it separately warns that long camera-roll uploads 'aren't prioritized by the Instagram Reels algorithm'. Multiple 2026 reel-length analyses converge on the same split between the 20-minute upload cap and the ~3-minute recommendation cutoff. Context: when Mosseri raised the cap to three minutes in January 2025 he said Instagram was 'still focused on short form video over long form'. No Meta primary source states the 3-minute recommendation cutoff as a number, so treat the exact ceiling as directional and the direction — shorter earns more cold reach — as well supported. Added this pass because the playbook previously carried no guidance on Reel length at all.

rules.title: Audio on a published feed post or carousel can now be replaced in place — never delete-and-repost just to change a song
rules.action: Swap the track with Replace Audio instead of deleting and re-uploading the post
rules.rule: Since 21 July 2026, rolled out globally, published feed posts and photo/video carousels can have their audio swapped without being taken down: open the post, tap More options, tap Edit, choose a new track, tap Done. The post keeps its existing likes, comments, shares and reach. Use it when a track was muted or cleared wrong, when a demo should be replaced by the released master, or when an older post should now carry the current single — instead of deleting and re-uploading, which throws away the post's accumulated engagement and adds another near-duplicate upload against the originality checks in ig-04. Replacement tracks come from Instagram's licensed library, and professional/business accounts see a filtered set of commercially cleared tracks, so confirm the intended track is available on Meghan's Page-linked account before planning a swap around a release date. The feature covers feed posts and carousels — not Reels.
rules.insight: Changing the song on a post no longer costs it its engagement history, which makes the old delete-and-repost workaround both unnecessary and actively harmful under Instagram's originality checks.
rules.evidence: Fast Company reported the global rollout on 21 July 2026: the 'Replace Audio' tool 'lets users update the music on their published posts at any time while keeping the post's existing likes, comments, shares, and reach intact', with the step-by-step flow and a link to Instagram's own help page (help.instagram.com/570998714799168). Instagram's @creators account announced the feature the same week, and SocialBee's Instagram update log records it under July 2026 as 'Instagram now allows users to change the music on any post'. Coverage consistently scopes it to published feed posts and carousels, with replacement tracks drawn from the licensed library and business accounts limited to commercially cleared tracks. Note the reach-preservation claim is Instagram's own framing as relayed by Fast Company; no independent measurement of post-swap distribution exists yet, so the safe reading is that the post and its history survive the swap, not that the swap earns new distribution.

rules.title: Ranking runs on total watch time including replays, not raw views — a short Reel rewatched beats a long one watched once
rules.action: Cut Reels short enough to loop — roughly 7-15 seconds unless the length earns itself
rules.rule: Stop optimizing for view count and start optimizing for seconds watched. Instagram counts total watch time including replays, so a 15-second Reel watched three times outranks a 60-second Reel watched once. Keep most Reels in the 7-15 second range, and make the last beat flow back into the first so the loop feels intentional rather than abrupt — a chorus line that lands on the downbeat it started on, a lyric that resolves into its own opening. Reserve longer cuts for content that genuinely holds (a full song, a story worth sitting through), and check average watch time and replays in Insights rather than plays. This sits underneath ig-11: ig-11 sets the outer ceiling for cold reach (~3 minutes), this rule sets the working target inside it.
rules.insight: Instagram ranks on total seconds watched including replays, which is why 7-15 second Reels outperform: they are easier to finish and easier to loop. Replay rate now sits alongside shares, watch-through rate, and saves as a top-tier signal.
rules.evidence: Multiple independent 2026 analyses report that Instagram's ranking shifted away from 3-second view counts to total watch time plus replay rate, with the worked example that a 15-second Reel watched three times outranks a 60-second Reel watched once. A separate 2026 Reels-specific breakdown ranks the most impactful signals as shares, watch-through rate, saves, and replay rate roughly in that order, and reports that 7-15 second Reels outperform longer ones because loop completion is read as high engagement. Re-verified 2026-09-06 against two further 2026 syntheses that state average watch completion rate is now the primary Reels ranking metric — one giving the worked example that a Reel watched by 10,000 people who all stop at 3 seconds performs worse than one watched by 1,000 people who finish and replay it — and that the current signal order is watch time and completion first, then sends per reach, then likes per reach. This is a refinement of the watch-time signal already referenced in ig-01, not a contradiction of it. Provenance note: this describes a state in effect through 2026 rather than a change published in the last month; it is recorded here because prior passes captured watch time only in passing and never as actionable guidance on Reel length or looping. Carried forward and renumbered from the unmerged 2026-08-13 pass, where it was drafted as ig-11 and collided with the 2026-08-18 ig-11. Re-verified 2026-09-08: further 2026 syntheses restate average watch completion rate as the primary Reels ranking metric and add skip rate (share of viewers scrolling past within the first 3 seconds) as a hook diagnostic now visible in Reels Insights. Skip rate is a measurement surface, not a confirmed ranking signal, and is deliberately not written in as one.

rules.title: Facebook Events are still the strongest native tool for live-show promotion, and RSVP activity compounds through social proof
rules.action: Create a Facebook Event for every show and tag the venue
rules.rule: Create a public Facebook Event for every show, tag the venue and any co-billed artists, and post show-specific, city-named updates in the week before ('Can't wait to play [City] on Friday'). Ask co-billed artists to cross-promote — a 3-artist bill that cross-promotes can triple each artist's individual reach. Ask fans to tap 'Interested' as well as 'Going' — the Events discovery surface weights prior interest signals, not just confirmed RSVPs.
rules.insight: Facebook Events are the strongest native tool for show promotion — RSVP activity compounds through social proof, and a cross-promoting co-bill can triple reach. Facebook's local Events discovery weights the artists a user follows, the events they have marked 'interested,' their location, and their friends' activity — so an 'Interested' tap is itself a distribution signal, not just a soft maybe.
rules.evidence: Two independent musician-marketing sources (Chartlex, Eventbrite/Yapsody-style guides) converge on Facebook Events as the standout native format for show promotion, citing the RSVP-to-network-visibility mechanic as a compounding, algorithm-friendly signal, plus explicit local-area Events-tab discovery surfacing. rules.evidence: Corroborated by two independent 2026 Facebook-algorithm breakdowns describing Meta's continued 'Meaningful Social Interactions' emphasis: posts sparking back-and-forth discussion and shares are favored, while low-effort/bait interactions contribute less to reach than in past years. rules.title: Facebook's unconnected-recommendation surface is large and growing — cold discovery on Facebook is real, and Reels are the way into it
rules.action: Stop treating Facebook as network-only — post Reels built for strangers, not just for people who already know her
rules.rule: Do not assume a Facebook post can only reach people who already follow the Page. Meta's own Q2 2026 transparency data puts unconnected in-Feed recommendations at 36.6% of US Feed content views, against 49.6% from friends, Groups and Public Followers — so roughly a third of what the average person sees on Facebook comes from sources they do not follow. Short-form video is the main way into that surface: Reels are distributed to non-followers at materially higher rates than static posts, and performance with a small test audience, not Page follower count, is what decides whether distribution expands. Practically, for a 2,961-follower Page: keep making Facebook Events and local, warm, relationship-driven posts (fb-02, fb-05), but stop reserving discovery-oriented Reels for Instagram alone — post the same clean, watermark-free Reel natively to Facebook too, and judge it on non-follower reach in Page Insights rather than assuming there is none to get.
rules.insight: Roughly a third of the average Facebook Feed is now recommended content from unfollowed sources, so Facebook is no longer a network-only channel — Reels are the entry point to that surface, and reach is decided by early performance rather than by follower count.
rules.evidence: This rule previously said the opposite, on a single medium-to-low-confidence industry synthesis, and was flagged as a watch item by the 2026-08-18 pass. It is now reversed on primary-source data. Meta's Widely Viewed Content Report for Q2 2026 reports that of US Feed content views, 49.6% came from posts shared by friends, Groups people had joined, or Public Followers; 36.6% came from in-Feed recommendations, which Meta defines as 'content from sources they are not connected to... we refer to this content as unconnected posts'; and the remaining 13.8% from less common products such as Events plus logging discrepancies. Mark Zuckerberg has separately put AI-recommended content at about 30% of Feed. Independent 2026 syntheses converge on the same direction and add the mechanism: Reels are distributed to non-followers at significantly higher rates than static posts, and content is no longer capped by follower count — strong performance with a small test audience triggers expansion to people who have never seen the Page. Note the direction of travel cuts both ways: the same reports describe continued long-term decline in organic Page reach through the Feed's connected half, which is why this rule pushes Reels specifically rather than Page posting in general. Confidence raised low -> medium: the headline share is Meta's own published figure, but it measures the whole US Feed, not this Page, and no Facebook-vs-Instagram non-follower comparison with primary sourcing was found — so the old claim is retired as unsupported rather than replaced by a quantified reversal.

rules.title: Facebook now explicitly demotes reaction clips, stitches, and add-nothing narration — genuine on-screen creative value is required, not just an original account uploading
rules.action: Never post a reaction/stitch clip without adding real commentary or new info
rules.rule: Don't post reaction videos, clip-stitches, or narration-over-existing-footage that doesn't add meaningful new value. If reposting or building on third-party clips (e.g., reacting to a review of a show or a fan-filmed clip), pair it with genuine analysis, new information, or a story improvement — plain reactions or narrating what's already visible get deprioritized in both Feed and Reels, and repeated unoriginal posting risks the account being marked non-recommendable.
rules.insight: Meta's own March 2026 policy explicitly deprioritizes reaction clips and stitches without added commentary — original Reels saw roughly double the watch time in H2 2025 versus H2 2024.
rules.evidence: Meta's official blog (about.fb.com, March 2026) states Facebook's ranking systems classify simply watching along, reacting with facial expressions, stitching clips together, or narrating on-screen content without meaningful addition as unoriginal, and deprioritize it across both Feed and Reels recommendations; consistently unoriginal accounts risk demonetization and being marked non-recommendable. The same post reports views and watch time for original Reels roughly doubled in H2 2025 vs H2 2024, corroborated by third-party trade coverage (Social Media Examiner, ALM Corp).

divergences.instagram: Instagram's Explore/Reels systems actively push content to non-followers via a staged trial funnel (Trial Reels, sequential test windows), making it the stronger channel for reaching people who have never heard of Meghan — especially younger, out-of-market fans.
divergences.facebook: Facebook's ranking model still leans on existing relationships and Meaningful Social Interactions for the connected half of Feed, but Meta's own Q2 2026 data puts unconnected in-Feed recommendations at 36.6% of US Feed content views — so cold discovery on Facebook is real, and Reels are the surface that reaches it (fb-06, revised 2026-09-06). Organic Page reach through connected Feed continues to decline; the discovery upside is in short-form video, not in Page posts.
divergences.recommendation: Use Instagram as the primary discovery/growth engine (new fans, younger audience, cold reach) and Facebook as the primary conversion/retention engine (show RSVPs, ticket sales, deepening relationships with the existing Front Range fanbase and 35+ core demographic) — but no longer treat Facebook as network-only. Post the same clean, watermark-free Reel natively to both apps and read non-follower reach in Page Insights before deciding Facebook cannot find new people.

divergences.instagram: Skews younger (Reels interactions concentrated in 18-34), better for reaching new/out-of-market listeners and building a national/touring fanbase over time.
divergences.facebook: Skews notably older (growing share above 35, especially 65+), a strong demographic match for country/Americana and for the local Colorado ticket-buying audience.
divergences.recommendation: Don't treat the two platforms as the same audience with two upload buttons. Consider genre-appropriate content splits: Facebook can carry more local-show-specific, direct 'buy tickets/RSVP' messaging aimed at an older, already-warm audience; Instagram should lean more on discovery-oriented, shareable 'bridge' content aimed at growing the base.

divergences.topic: Native Reels vs. cross-posted Reels performance
divergences.instagram: No independent-source data was found directly quantifying native-IG-Reel vs. cross-posted-from-elsewhere performance differences on Instagram itself beyond the general originality/repost penalty (ig-04, ig-07) — the penalty is about detectable staleness/watermarks, not the act of cross-posting per se.
divergences.facebook: One source states Facebook's algorithm gives 'user-generated'/original Reels roughly 3.2x more organic reach than content repurposed from other platforms, and separately confirms same-video, watermark-free cross-posting between IG and FB itself carries no penalty.
divergences.recommendation: The clearest, best-supported version of 'native beats cross-posted' is about removing third-party watermarks and avoiding stale/recycled reposts — not about whether the same clean video is shared to both IG and FB. Post the same clean Reel natively to both apps (not routed through a TikTok-style badge or auto-poster that leaves a watermark), and treat the underlying originality of the footage, not the platform-to-platform sharing itself, as the primary reach factor. This finding is graded medium confidence — the 3.2x figure comes from a single source (autofaceless.ai) and was not independently corroborated with a second source; treat the ratio itself as directional, not precise.

divergences.instagram: External links in captions face a measurable reach penalty (est. 19-60% reduction depending on source); links belong in bio or Stories stickers.
divergences.facebook: No comparable link-penalty pattern was found in Facebook-specific 2026 sources; Facebook Events (which function as a structured, algorithm-favored 'link') and direct ticket/venue links in posts are treated as normal, expected content, especially for show promotion.
divergences.recommendation: Be link-shy on Instagram (bio/Stories only); be comfortable posting direct ticket links, venue links, and Event links in Facebook posts and Event descriptions, since Facebook's local-event discovery mechanics are built around exactly this kind of structured, linked content.

postingWindows.instagram: Updated 2026-08-18 against Buffer's refreshed benchmark study (updated July 2026, 9.6 million Instagram posts from 200,000+ accounts, part of its State of Social Engagement 2026 report). Headline windows, in the poster's own local time: Thursday 9am is the single strongest slot, followed by Wednesday 12pm and Wednesday 6pm; the broader bands that work for most accounts are 7-9am, 11am-1pm and 6-9pm local. Because the study normalises to local time, these read straight across to America/Denver with no ET-to-MT conversion — which supersedes the previous entry's inferred '5-7pm MT, converted from a 7-9pm ET data point'. Practical recommendation for Meghan: lead with Thursday morning (~9am MT) and Wednesday midday/early evening, keep the 6-9pm MT band for Reels aimed at the after-work scroll, and pair a show-announcement post with the morning slot rather than late night. One caveat carried forward: a separate reverse-engineered 2026 study found Monday the best day and Tuesday the worst, which conflicts with Buffer's Thursday/Wednesday finding — the two used different methods and neither is Meta-primary, so treat day-of-week as the weakest part of this guidance and let Instagram's own 'Best Time to Post' insight in the Professional Dashboard override both once the account has enough native data.
postingWindows.facebook: No Facebook-specific, timezone-granular 'best time to post' dataset was found with strong sourcing in this research pass; general social-media benchmark guides bundle Facebook into cross-platform 'weekday 9am-1pm and 7-9pm' windows without Facebook-specific music-audience data. Given Facebook's older, local, event-driven audience for Meghan, the most defensible approach (medium/low confidence, inferred rather than directly sourced) is to post show-specific and Event-linked content in early-to-mid evening Mountain time (roughly 6-8pm MT) on weekdays, when an older local audience is likely browsing after work, and to post Event updates 2 weeks out and again in the final week before a show, per the two-touch cadence recommended in musician-specific FB Events guides.
